sources.north_label_text: Graticule ticks labelled 70°12'15"E to 70°13'05"E and 23°52'.."N along the map frame; also an eight-point rose lettered N, E, S, W

north_arrow_measurement.description: North taken from the plan's graticule: each pair of longitude ticks on the top and bottom of the map frame marks a meridian. All eleven pairs are offset by 17.5 to 18.5 px over the 2106 px between the tick rows (mean 17.77 px), so the meridians lean 0.48 deg anticlockwise from the frame, which is what the UTM zone 42 grid convergence predicts at this longitude. The plan's eight-point rose, about 175 px tip to tip, leans by a similar amount.

rendering_check.note: A GIS map embedded as a raster at native resolution. The map frame is square (top and bottom frame rows constant across the sheet) and the latitude ticks on the left and right frame give parallels turned by the same 0.5 deg as the meridians, so the graticule is internally consistent. We assume 0.1 deg.

sources.notes: The plan shows terrain contours from a 2019-20 survey, not walls; we measured the long straight edges of the castle and Middle Town mounds where contours bunch along buried or exposed wall faces. Lengths are those of the contour edges, which run inside or outside the wall faces by a few metres.

main_system_reason: The contour plan is the only measured plan whose north is defined by a geographic graticule rather than a drawn arrow, and its castle and Middle Town edges agree with each other within about one degree. The three drafted plans place the same walls six to eight degrees to either side of their own arrows, so their arrows, not the walls, are the uncertain element.
notes: We measured four plans. The first is the ASI's 2020 contour survey of the site (UNESCO document 184544, drawing of 0.5 m contours), which carries a latitude-longitude graticule; we took north from its meridians and measured the straight mound edges along the castle and Middle Town walls. The other three are drafted plans with drawn compass roses and no stated kind of north: the city-wide 'ratio and proportions' plan of the 2020 nomination dossier (Fig. 2.10), the castle plan reproduced in Bisht's 2015 preliminary report (Fig. 6.3), and the dossier's redrawing of that castle plan with a new rose (Fig. 2.11). All four were measured on the embedded images at native resolution. On the contour plan the castle and Middle Town edges lie within about one degree of the meridian. On the two castle plans the castle walls are turned clockwise from the drawn rose by six to eight degrees, and on the city plan every fortification line, the castle included, is turned anticlockwise from its rose by about seven and a half degrees. The walls are square to each other on every plan, so the disagreement lies in where the roses were drawn; the graticule settles it in favour of the contour plan, and we report the drafted plans as separate systems. Most of the outer and Middle Town fortification on the 2020 drafted plans is drawn as conjectural lines joining confirmed stretches and corners, so those lines give the direction between confirmed points. The ASI A3 drawing sheets also carry a standard north symbol in the title block that is square to the sheet whatever the plan's own rose shows; we did not use it. The dossier's street plan (Fig. 2.93) and the 100 m grid plan (Fig. 2.7, Bisht Fig. 4.1) have no north arrow of their own and were not measured.
